records.name: Scoped accessibility, contact and expression profiles
openObligations: Adult male 8-10-week C57BL/6-background mice; rapidly dissected bulk dentate gyri enriched in neurons, not purified neurons or single-cell measurements. ECS is induced synchronous activation, not an explicit learning task or a measured sustained cognitive state.

ATAC-seq and RNA-seq use independent samples. GEO GSE82015 lists four wild-type ATAC replicates at E0/E1/E4 and two sh-cFos E1 ATAC replicates; other AAV ATAC groups and RNA groups have three. GSE86367 lists three E24 ATAC and three RNA samples. Replicate labels do not independently verify animal identity or sample independence.

c-Fos knockdown uses one shRNA and overexpression uses AAV2/9 one week before assay. No reviewed rescue with a second sequence excludes all off-target effects. External KCl-neuron ChIP-seq annotations are not matched in vivo c-Fos occupancy measurements.

A 1/4/24-hour comparison across sacrificed cohorts does not demonstrate persistence in the same cell, lifelong memory, inheritance or a universal minimal assembly. RNA abundance is distinct from transcription rate, protein output and behavioral function.

Figure 6c has a 144/114 gene-count conflict. Figure 7c caption says E0/E4/E24, while plot and experimental text specify E0/E1/E4. Supplementary Tables 4-5 contain conflicting headers, nonfinite values or spreadsheet errors. No global quantitative model is calibrated from these data.

The main Methods report no sample-size predetermination, randomization or blinding. Some qPCR primer labels/sequences conflict. Published findings, metadata inspection and source-cell counts are not independent biological replication or sequencing-pipeline reproduction.

Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Marker selection, reporter maturation and a roughly 12-hour labeling window limit cell identity and temporal specificity.

Whole-hippocampus molecular samples pool nuclei across animals and neuronal subtypes. ATAC Methods specify 10,000 nuclei from 8-10 mice per replicate. Table 13 lists three Basal and four Late libraries, while the reporting summary excludes one Basal from 13 and Figure 2a states n=3 per group. The included-library mapping remains unresolved. A library, genomic locus, slice or punctum is not an independent animal. Destructive cohorts are not single-cell longitudinal measurements.

Figure 1f counts are labeled cells per DG slice; the caption refers to hippocampus. Its five versus six mice each contribute six sections, while tests report df=59/57. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. Animal-level effects and confidence intervals require source measurements and sample reconciliation.

Hi-C Methods describe two libraries per Basal, Early and Late population, but the reporting summary excludes one Early library. Methods say two animals per sample, whereas reporting specifies four to five. Promoter-capture Hi-C covers four populations and selected promoters. Contact frequencies and inferred A/B compartments are not unique three-dimensional coordinates. Figure 3 specifies a 500-kb Juicer representation, while Methods and software use 50-kb HOMER compartment PCA; their mapping needs explicit reconstruction.

ATAC Figure 2a labels log2 fold-change thresholds, while its caption, Methods and software say fold changes >1.5. RNA Table 8 has undocumented sign reorientation and a near-threshold extra row. The RNA Methods cite an edgeR reference for DESeq2 and the software omits the RNA export code. No sequence analysis, signed gene-specific pathway or edge weight is calibrated.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues. Sequencing sample sizes used observed variability and group differences; ATAC/Hi-C quality exclusions and a plotted ATAC outlier exclusion were not pre-established. Normality was assumed without formal testing. Null tests are not equivalence tests. Separate molecular profiles and behavioral outcomes do not establish a chromatin-to-memory mediation chain or lifelong persistence.

Accessibility and contact-frequency profiles are not direct chromatin-density, unique three-dimensional packing, mechanical force or molecular remodeling trajectories. RNA abundance is not a transcription rate or a direct replication/repair-permissibility measurement.

Separate profiles and populations do not establish that packing causes the expression differences. c-Fos perturbation has multiple possible routes; matching ATAC/RNA effects does not uniquely identify accessibility as their mediator.

Population-level region overlap through sampled windows is not an inherited state, a persistent same-cell trajectory, a universal physical sequence-to-functional-resource transformation or complete spatial control of genomic function.

The original epigenetic, nucleic-acid copying, hydrogen-bond and signal-pathway parents are separate scopes. A named chromatin role does not make them necessary causal ancestors or substitute for a matched packaging intervention.

Source catalogue level, phase, role, science/status and requirement labels are representation choices. Original parent weights, necessity, directions/modes, carrier minima/critical counts and null saturation are not measured causal fractions, physical thresholds or a universal construction sequence. Generic evidence placeholders add no unidentified study or independent replication.

openObligations: Read the complete published primary article pages 936-947, complete PMC main HTML and all seven main figures/captions. The author-lab PDF has a graphical cover plus twelve published pages. Read selected actual 29-page publisher supplement: title page, Figure S4 page 5, Figure S7 pages 10-11, Section S2 relevant in vitro/FRAP pages 14-16, Section S6 pages 21-25, and Section S8 pages 27-28. Other SI preparation/statistical/genome-analysis pages, full sequence details, raw data and movies were not completely read.

Ddx4N1 is the supplied isolated disordered N-terminal region (residues 1-236), without the central DEAD-box helicase. Ddx4YFP replaces that helicase with YFP, and cellular/full-length constructs differ. In vitro terminal-region phase separation is not a demonstration of native germ-granule function, helicase catalysis or a universal folded-protein prerequisite.

Thermal Figure 3D reports 202 micromolar Ddx4N1, 200 mM NaCl and pH 8, with cooling/heating and same-sample repeats. Its 4 degrees C/min demonstration differs from the 2 degrees C/min default cloud-point sampling in SI Section S6. Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

Cloud-point data and Flory-Huggins/screened-Coulomb fits are separate from direct images. Assumptions about polymer volume fraction, water, effective interaction constants and electrostatic screening underlie fitted enthalpy/entropy, charge spacing and dielectric values. No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

FRAP main Figure 3C describes a 60:1 Ddx4N1:Ddx4YFP mixture; SI pages 15-16 instead list pre-dilution concentrations 292.5 micromolar Ddx4N1 and 8.1 micromolar each YFP construct and free CFP, with hanging-drop equilibration. No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

Thermal Figure 3D reports 202 micromolar Ddx4N1, 200 mM NaCl and pH 8, with cooling/heating and same-sample repeats. Its 4 degrees C/min demonstration differs from the 2 degrees C/min default cloud-point sampling in SI Section S6. Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

Cloud-point data and Flory-Huggins/screened-Coulomb fits are separate from direct images. Assumptions about polymer volume fraction, water, effective interaction constants and electrostatic screening underlie fitted enthalpy/entropy, charge spacing and dielectric values. No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

FRAP main Figure 3C describes a 60:1 Ddx4N1:Ddx4YFP mixture; SI pages 15-16 instead list pre-dilution concentrations 292.5 micromolar Ddx4N1 and 8.1 micromolar each YFP construct and free CFP, with hanging-drop equilibration. No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

The partition experiment uses source-defined 32-base single-stranded or 32-base-paired double-stranded fluorescent DNA at equal nominal fluorophore concentration in a separate Ddx4N1 preparation. Background-subtracted emission per region volume is a concentration/partition proxy; equal quantum yield/dye behavior across phases and free-energy calibration are not independently verified.

The source defines its partition coefficient as outside/inside, not the inverse. The main Results paragraph names atto657N whereas Figure 7 and Experimental Procedures name Atto647N. No numerical partition/free-energy value, unlabeled-DNA binding constant, universal sequence specificity or corrected dye identity is independently admitted.

Ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields of view are sampling regions, not automatically sixty independent preparation replications. SD of emission regions and model-fit SE are different uncertainties. No independent replication or raw-image replay is performed.

Cellular cold/osmotic response, methylated/splice/charge/aromatic variants and genome enrichment were read but are not new admitted assay contexts. Cellular osmotic changes alter volume/concentration and environment together; sequence/general-mechanism hypotheses do not become universal proof for all condensates.

The admitted thermal, FRAP and DNA-partition contexts do not directly resolve fusion or fission dynamics, transfer/exchange rates for every component or one unique intermolecular/solvent mechanism. No direct catalytic reaction modulation, metabolic throughput/benefit, universal reaction sequestration, membrane-like selectivity, gradient maintenance, prebiotic coacervate ancestry or origin-of-life event is measured in the admitted contexts.
Source fits, calibration and raw measurements are not independently reconstructed or reproduced.

openObligations: This source studies an expressed, purified His6-tagged E. coli CAP N-terminal fragment comprising residues1-138. It lacks the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of full-length CAP; no DNA binding, transcription, catalytic turnover, cellular adaptation or physiological response is measured in this selected study.

The protein is supplied as a prepared homodimer. Its composition and two cAMP-binding positions are system-specific inputs/assignments, not a universal two-molecule threshold or proof that all allostery requires oligomerization.

The source supplies a ligand-series experiment at30C and fixed assay protocols. It does not measure a universal folding, hydrogen-bond, electrostatic, hydration or feedback ancestry, and it does not operationalize original parent weights or carrier minima.

The supporting information, raw NMR/ITC acquisition, complete concentration calibration, original fitting implementation and covariance are not independently reviewed or reproduced. All admitted quantities retain publication-supported status.

Figure7 constants are source sequential-binding fit parameters, not a Hill coefficient, direct atom-count measurement or new microscopic site-specific constants. Sequential constants require their combinatorial/state convention before translating them into intrinsic coupling energies; no statistical-factor correction is newly calculated here.

A biphasic isotherm or nonlinearity alone does not uniquely establish intersite communication rather than fixed site heterogeneity. The source interpretation also uses the symmetric-dimer preparation and site-resolved ligand-series NMR.

The reported0.04 and4micromolar constants have no printed uncertainty in Figure7; none is invented. The100-fold ratio and rounded thermodynamic entries are source statements, not a new fit or uncertainty reconstruction.

The main manuscript gives protein concentrations without a separately reconstructed monomer/dimer concentration calibration. Its intended dimer ligation states are retained, but the Figure7 molar-ratio axis is not used as an independent site-count determination.

Nominal cAMP:CAPN dimer ratios1:1 and2:1 enrich the source-assigned ligation states; finite affinities and stoichiometric mixing do not demonstrate mathematically pure occupancy populations. The source complete-saturation phrasing is not promoted to a new measured purity guarantee.
